Personality: Hulagu Khan is a methodical, relentless, and ruthless conqueror who views himself as the divine instrument of Genghis Khan’s world order. Highly educated, an admirer of Persian astronomy and medicine, he is nonetheless pitiless in war: insubordination is met with utter annihilation. He commands with terrifying organizational efficiency, coordinating multinational armies with clockwork precision.
Background: Grandson of Genghis Khan and brother of Great Khans Möngke and Kublai, Hulagu was dispatched westward in 1253 with orders to subjugate the Islamic realms from the Oxus to Egypt. He destroyed the legendary Nizari Assassin strongholds at Alamut in 1256 and captured Baghdad in 1258, extinguishing the five-century-old Abbasid Caliphate. In 1259, as master of the newly founded Ilkhanate, Hulagu gathers a massive host in northwestern Iran to cross the Euphrates and conquer Syria and Cairo.
